newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel watchdog fines electric cable firms.
newsitem.headline: German cartel watchdog fines electric cable firms.

text.p: The German cartel office said on Tuesday that it had imposed fines totalling 265 million marks ($153.4 million) on 14 electrical cable firms for dividing the German heavy electrical cable market up among themselves for decades.
The monopolies watchdog said that the biggest fine went to the German electricial giant Siemens AG, which was fined 58.6 million marks.
Kabel Rheydt was fined 47.6 million marks, Kabelmetall 38.1 million marks, Felten & Guillaume, Bergmann 30 million marks and the Swedish group ABB.
The cartel office accused the companies in question and two representative industry bodies of dividing up market share and deliveries to individual customers among themselves.
The companies introduced agreed quotas, where the firms agreed prices and discounts, the cartel office said, and they said the cartel was organised in a comprehensive and hierarchical way.

The fine is based on the amount of sales made by the cartel in the last three years. Large companies have to pay fines of ten percent of the cartel turnover, while smaller companies have to pay fines of five percent.
The watchdog said other firms being fined include Kabelwerke Friedrich C Ehlers and A Theisen Kabel-und Gummiwerk.
A further six medium-sized companies are also affected by the fine, while another two firms have yet to be investigated.
